rationale: Evidence from iteration 4 (score 56.11, the best so far): the oval now shows 0 line-loss events and progress 0.137 (up from 0.124), but max_error is 0.0605, still just over the 0.06 m off-track limit. On s-bend and slalom, line_loss_events stayed at 1 with search_right, and progress was unchanged (0.1576 and 0.1099). The search direction therefore did not change where the line is lost. The Evaluator's conditions are both met: (1) oval max_error is at or above 0.06 with sensor_size 0.016, so base_speed drops from 1.4 to 1.2 to give slower entry into the first corner; (2) s-bend and slalom line-loss events stayed at 1 with search_right, so line_loss changes to search_left with the same geometry. Geometry is unchanged: five sensors at x = -0.05, -0.025, 0, 0.025, 0.05 m, y = 0.04 m, sensor_size 0.016, and the same body, wheel and mass values. kp 4.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.30 and the sensor weights are also unchanged. Expected result: oval max_error falls below 0.06 with 0 line losses, and s-bend and slalom line-loss events drop to 0 or the progress values change, which will show whether the loss point depends on search direction. Risk: two controller fields change at once (speed and recovery direction). Speed mainly affects the oval, and direction mainly affects s-bend and slalom, so the per-track telemetry should separate them. Hypotheses to check: (a) base_speed 1.2 brings oval max_error below 0.06 while progress stays at or above 0.124; (b) search_left reduces or keeps the s-bend and slalom line-loss count at 1 with different progress; (c) steering_oscillation stays near 0.15. If progress falls on all tracks, speed 1.2 is too slow and should return to 1.4.
